observations: Multiple batteries in retail packaging stacked in a warehouse or shop setting.
The boxes are labeled 'SAHARA ENERGY' in large text.
The specification '12V 250AH' is clearly printed on the front of the boxes.
The text 'CARBON BATTERY' and 'TALL TUBULAR BATTERY' is visible on the packaging.
A watermark for 'SOLAR WORLD' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' is overlaid on the image.
The batteries appear to be wrapped in factory plastic.

claims.evidence: The packaging matches the brand, but the authenticity of the internal components cannot be verified from a photo of a box.
The performance and health of chemical batteries require physical testing (load test, voltage check) which cannot be done remotely.

risks.risk: The batteries may be old stock with significant self-discharge or sulfation.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturing date stamp or code on the battery casing (not the box).

risks.risk: The battery may be dead or unable to hold a charge (internal cell failure).
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading of the open-circuit voltage and a load test showing stable voltage under discharge.

proof_requests: Photo of the manufacturing date stamp on the actual battery casing.
Video of a multimeter reading the voltage of a randomly selected unit from the stack.
Close-up photo of the terminals to check for signs of previous use or corrosion.
response.reason: The brand and model are clearly identified from the retail packaging. It can be priced at the market rate for this specific model, though it must be valued at its worst case (non-functional/scrap) until health is proven.
